_doc: The realm's household guard (player/realmEscort.js): a lord, a great lord or the crown rides with an escort the realm keeps. Its men are drawn out of the realm's own army (kingdom.military; never more than maxShare of it at once) and go back to it when the escort ends; each company is armed out of the realm's armoury (kingdom.armoury.stock: a piece for each slot of its kit, a quiver of arrows for its bowmen) and hands back what the survivors carry. The crown pays them: each company's wage (its unit type's upkeep x pay.mult) out of the treasury daily, booked on the crown's 'guard' line, into the men's pockets (spent in the towns they lodge in, pay.spendShare a day; what is left goes home with them to the capital); their bread is bought from a town's granary as the army's is (supply), the crown paying the town. What the treasury cannot pay is owed: morale falls, and after arrears.graceDays the unpaid slip away (their arms with them). The fallen are the realm's dead and their kits are lost with them. A rank: crown (the player rules the realm), great (Chancellor, the Great Lord start's House in its realm, or greatEstates estates there), lord (a Lord's office - Marshal, Spymaster - or lordEstates estates in the realm one is sworn to). units: the companies the rank rides with; extra: how many more the crown may send when asked (extraUnit each); refill: one lost company replaced every refill.days while the treasury and the army allow. ask: what asking for more costs (reputation with the realm, never below ask.minReputation; a ruler pays nothing) and the treasury it must hold after (reserveBase + reserveDays of the guard's wage). sendHome: days before a guard sent home is sent again unasked. deserted: days before a guard whose last man deserted (starved or unpaid) is sent again unasked. loyalty: grows with days served and victories; at coupJoinAt or more the guard joins a general's coup, below it stands with the crown. deter: bands in sight are less eager to set on a party in a crown's livery (military.json encounters.pursuit.escortMult); a rival's thieves and assassins striking at you meet the guard (schemeFoil chances).

fight._doc: On the street map the guard fights at your side (ui/innerMapEscort.js): the beast you fight or that is charging or attacking you, and whoever is fighting you (never an arena bout or a job duel, and never the law: the town watch, the gaoler or a castle guard, it stands aside). Each figure closes in and strikes every swingEvery seconds (a little off the beat of the others) for its company type's damage; joinRange: how many tiles from you a foe may be for them to go to it; reach: tiles from the foe a blow lands.
fight._companions: Your travelling companions (ui/innerMapCompanions.js) fight beside you against the same foes, by the same rules: each blow base + their role's battle power (PlayerEffects.companionRole: a general 0.12, a knight 0.10, a guard 0.06...) x perPower, times their mood and bonds (Companions.effectiveness).
